story.head: The Kings shut down the dangerous stuff, the Sharks don’t
paras: The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in overtime in San Jose on Oct 3. The Sharks (7-6-1) beat Vancouver 3-2 on Thursday, and the Kings (4-6-2) beat Ottawa 6-5 in overtime the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Sharks fourth (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh (tied for 28th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Sharks’ record (.536) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.386), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Kings have played better than their record (.417) says: their chances are worth about .573, and their finishing has held them back.

The Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd), do a lot of their shooting from distance (4th lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). The Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest), take away shots from the point (4th lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Kings keep dangerous shots away, but the Sharks give up a lot of them.

Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 12 GP) is carrying the Sharks’ offense, and Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 14 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 5 A / 13 P in 12 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven goals in seven games against San Jose since 2023-24.

Yaroslav Askarov (4-5-0 / .900 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for San Jose. Los Angeles has two options in net: Darcy Kuemper (4-3-1 / .878 SV% in 8 GS) and Anton Forsberg (0-3-1 / .902 SV% in 4 GS). Kuemper has started seven of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday, so Los Angeles could turn to Forsberg to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: The Sharks are newly without Igor Chernyshov, and have been without Alexander Wennberg since Oct 19.

The Kings are newly without Brandt Clarke and Mats Zuccarello, have been without Alex Turcotte since Oct 6, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
Adam Gaudette has a point in four straight games against Los Angeles, with a goal in each of the last three.
Adrian Kempe has three goals on chances worth about 6.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
